# hyperv_port_proxy (Resource)

**Requirements:** tested with the built-in `Administrator` account on Windows Server 2022 (build 10.0.20348); a less privileged identity hasn't been tested. The IP Helper service (`iphlpsvc`) must be running, because it owns every portproxy listener.

Manages one [`netsh interface portproxy`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows-server/networking/technologies/netsh/netsh-interface-portproxy) `v4tov4` rule, which forwards a TCP port on the host to an IPv4 address and port, plus an optional inbound firewall allow rule. It needs no `NetNat` instance, so it can forward to any address the host can reach. It forwards TCP only. For a guest behind a `NetNat`, typically on a `hyperv_virtual_switch` with `switch_type = "NAT"`, or for UDP, use `hyperv_nat_static_mapping` instead.

Create checks the port against `netsh interface ipv4 show excludedportrange protocol=tcp` and then confirms the IP Helper service is listening, because `netsh` accepts a rule for an excluded port without reporting an error. If either check fails, Create removes the rule.

A DHCP guest can come back with a different address after a host reboot. Set `connect_address` from the address the guest reports, for example `hyperv_vm.<x>.network_adapter[0].ip_addresses[0]`, and the next apply retargets the rule in place.

A rule on a specific `listen_address`, such as a DHCP address on an External switch's host vNIC, has come back from a host reboot with no listener while netsh still held it. Read then reports `listening = false`, and the next apply deletes and re-adds the rule. Rules on `0.0.0.0` kept listening across the same reboot, so prefer `0.0.0.0` unless the rule must listen on one host address.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Address the guest reports, for example
# hyperv_vm.controlplane.network_adapter[0].ip_addresses[0]. Feeding it in
# lets the next apply follow a new DHCP lease.
variable "controlplane_ip" {
  type = string
}

# Forward host port 15000 to the Talos API on the guest.
resource "hyperv_port_proxy" "talos_api" {
  listen_port     = 15000
  connect_address = var.controlplane_ip
  connect_port    = 50000
}

# Listen on one host address only, and manage the firewall rule under a
# chosen name on the Private profile.
resource "hyperv_port_proxy" "ssh" {
  listen_address  = "192.168.3.77"
  listen_port     = 2222
  connect_address = "172.30.98.10"
  connect_port    = 22

  firewall_rule = {
    name    = "lab-ssh"
    profile = "Private"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `connect_address` (String) IPv4 address to forward to, typically a guest's address. Updates in place.
- `connect_port` (Number) TCP port to forward to, 1 to 65535. Updates in place.
- `listen_port` (Number) Host TCP port to listen on, 1 to 65535. It must lie outside every Windows TCP exclusion range. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Optional

- `firewall_rule` (Attributes) Inbound firewall allow rule for `listen_port`. Defaults to `{ enabled = true, profile = "Any" }`, with `name` derived as `hyperv-pp-<listen_address>-<listen_port>`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--firewall_rule))
- `listen_address` (String) Host IPv4 address to listen on. Defaults to `0.0.0.0`, every address. Changing this forces a new resource.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier `<listen_address>:<listen_port>`, the key netsh stores the rule under.
- `listening` (Boolean) Whether the IP Helper service listens on `listen_address`:`listen_port`. Read reports `false` for a rule netsh holds with no listener, and the next apply re-adds the rule.

<a id="nestedatt--firewall_rule"></a>
### Nested Schema for `firewall_rule`

Optional:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether to manage a `NetFirewallRule` for the listen port. Defaults to `true`. With `false`, the port stays blocked unless another rule opens it.
- `name` (String) Firewall rule `DisplayName`. Defaults to `hyperv-pp-<listen_address>-<listen_port>`. Changing this forces a new resource.
- `profile` (String) Firewall profile: `Any`, `Domain`, `Private`, or `Public`. Defaults to `Any`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import a rule by its listen address and port.
terraform import hyperv_port_proxy.example "0.0.0.0:15000"

# Add the firewall rule's name when it isn't the default hyperv-pp-<listen_address>-<listen_port>.
terraform import hyperv_port_proxy.example "192.168.3.77:2222:lab-ssh"
```
